I was taught and teach the four golden rules:

  1. Always treat a weapon like its loaded, or in other words, never assume a gun is clear & safe. Whenever you pick up a firearm, check to make sure the weapon is clear. Then check it again, and maybe a third time. When someone hands you a firearm, check to make sure the weapon is clear, even if they just did so before handing it to you.

  2. Never point the weapon at something or someone you don't want to shoot. This is pretty straight forward. Weapons are tools, not toys. Don't point a gun at someone as a joke, even if you cleared the weapon and know it's safe, as they won't know, and could react in ways you don't intend. Or you could have failed to properly clear the weapon, and are now endangering their life. Just don't do it.

  3. Keep your finger off the trigger until you are aiming at your target. Again this is straight forward. Most weapons will be designed with this rule in mind. There is usually a flat surface on the side of the weapon where you can rest your trigger finger when you are holding the weapon but not engaging a target.

  4. Be aware of what is in front of, behind, and to the side of your target. You can miss, something can move between you and the target, or your bullet can over penetrate, or the target itself can move, and you end up shooting someone you did not intend to.
